prompt: A $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle has hypotenuse $12$. Write the exact length of the longer leg (the side opposite the $60^\circ$ angle) in simplest radical form.
hint: In a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle the sides go short leg, short leg $\times \sqrt{3}$, short leg $\times 2$.

hints.text: In a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle the sides go short leg, short leg $\times \sqrt{3}$, short leg $\times 2$.
The hypotenuse is twice the short leg, so the short leg is $12 \div 2 = 6$.

explanation: Find the short leg first: it is always half the hypotenuse, so $12 \div 2 = 6$.
The longer leg is the short leg times $\sqrt{3}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Where the ratio comes from
steps: Fold an equilateral triangle of side $12$ in half — the fold is the height and you get a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle with hypotenuse $12$ and short leg $6$.
The fold line satisfies $6^2 + h^2 = 12^2$, so $h^2 = 108$ and $h = \sqrt{108} = 6\sqrt{3}$.
